title: Heap: top k largest
summary: The k largest values, largest first. Keep a min-heap of at most k values; its root is the smallest survivor, the bar a new value must beat. O(n log k).
code: # The smallest retained value stays at the heap root.
triggers: k largest, smallest, most frequent or closest
a stream where only the best k matter
prompts: A game server receives scores all day. Keep the ten highest scores so far without storing every score.
From thousands of delivery stops, return the five closest to the depot.
invariant: heap holds the k largest values seen so far, and heap[0] is the smallest of them.
mantra: Keep k in a min-heap; the root is the bar to beat.
pitfalls: heapq is min-only: push -value, or (-key, tiebreak, item), for a max-heap.
Tuples compare field by field; add an index tiebreak when items can't be compared.
Once the heap is full, heapq.heappushpop(heap, value) pushes and pops in one step.
Only heap[0] is ordered; sort the heap to return it in order.

anchors.name: Kth Largest Element in an Array
anchors.trick: Size-k min-heap; heap[0] is the answer.

anchors.name: Top K Frequent Elements
anchors.trick: Counter first, then a size-k heap of (count, value).

anchors.name: K Closest Points to Origin
anchors.trick: Size-k max-heap keyed by -(x * x + y * y); skip the square root.

anchors.name: Merge k Sorted Lists

mutations.explanation: Pops as soon as the heap reaches k, so only k - 1 values survive.
